items.text: Reijiro Wakat Wakatsuki, - suki, Wakatsuki, chief of the Japanese delegation to the London Naval Conference, it was learned today, couched his final reports following the signing of the naval limitations treaty in picturesque terms of humility, according to an ages old Oriental custom. Cabling Premier Hamaguchi, Wakatsuki laments his own “inadequate abilities,” professes to consider the results obtained on behalf of Japan (Continued on Page 3, Column 2.) Officials announced today that 12 insurgents were killed and two wounded seriously in a fight near Chittagong last night between the group which raided the Chittagbng police arsenal Saturday and British troops. Fourteen arrests were made. No soldiers were Injured. The insurgents were posted in a strong position on a hill and were attacted by detachments of the eastern frontier rifles and the Burma Valley light horse. The main body of the raiders still was at large following the engagement, but military operations were continuing. Indian Speaker to Resign. Nationalist

OP).—The Bombay Chronicle today said that the villagers at Raas, where Vallabhai Patel, brother of the speaker of the Indian Legislative Assembly, was arrested for his activities in behalf of the civil disobedience movement, had decided to refuse to pay any land taxes henceforth. British Soldier Is Killed. PESHAWAR, India, April 23 OP).—A British soldier was killed today during a disturbance over the arrest of a number of civil disobedience campaigners here. April 23 OP).— Ray Lyman Wilbur, Secretary of the Interior, and on leave as president of Stanford University, is seven times a grandfather. Mrs. Max Foster Hopper of Palo Alto, formerly Miss Lois Wilbur, has presented her family with a daughter, named Nancy Jane Hopper. LIGHT FROST AND

(A*).—Newspapers, which, in the words of a government spokesman, give excessive typographical emphasis and unjust abundance of details to news of airplane accidents are subject to sequestration. The penalty has been Imposed on some. All that is permitted is the mere announcement of a crash. “Wales Plane” Crashes. CAIRO, Egypt, April 23 (A 3 ).—The airplane on which the Prince of Wales traveled here from Khartum last week crashed this morning at Heliopolis Airdrome shortly after taking off on its return flight to Khartum. Ita occupants were killed. ■• -

BP). —The Leviathan sailed from Southampton harbor at 7:30 a.m. today, taking with It Col. Henry L. Stimson, American Secretary of State, and others of the American delegation to the London Naval Conference. Departure of the steamer was delayed more than 19 hours in order that the naval delegates might complete the work of the conference with signing of the treaty. They came aboard at midnight, after a rail trip from London, but the ship had to await letter tide conditions before attempting the difficult harbor channel. Accompanying Col. Stimson

with the Geneva Conference of 1927 and removal of Anglo-American shipbuilding rivalry are the points most stressed in today’s editorial comment on conclusion of the Naval Conference.
